summary: The pricing change is not in the code. routes/pricing/pricing.json has many old plans. It has no 20 USD plan and no 50 USD plan. It has no total discount limit. Paywalls are empty. Discount routes do not read the plan. test-prd.txt is not in the repo.

blastRadius.notes: routes/pricing/pricing.json holds the plans. Prices include 0, 19, and 49. The file has no price 20 and no price 50. Each plan paywalls object is empty. The field monthly_store_orders is absent.

routes/pricing/pricing.service.js creates Shopify recurring charges from pricing.json. It also creates a free subscription, an annual subscription, a usage charge, and a cancel. A missing plan name throws an error.
getPaywalls reads pricing.json paywalls. Those objects are empty. routes/pricing/paywall.json is not imported by any JS file. Its plan lists are empty.
The code has no total discount counter. users.counters stores modal counts only. shopOrdersCount stores a monthly order count. It does not store a discount count.
routes/orders/orders.controller.js reads monthly_store_orders. That field is not in pricing.json. The check does not stop the order. It sends a Slack note on each 100th order.
routes/orders/orders.service.js bills a percent from plan charges.value. Current plan charges.value is 0, except Yearly_Plus_19_FlyBundles which is 10. A zero amount skips the usage charge.
routes/discounts, routes/bundles, routes/volumeBundle, and routes/frequentBought do not read the plan. Shopify discount extensions do not read the plan.
frontend.service.js writes isSubscription.name into the theme script. Theme widgets do not block offers by plan price.
Revenue cron jobs filter users by isSubscription.name. They list old plan names such as Free_Plan_Sept_2025. They do not list a 20 USD plan or a 50 USD plan.
This repo has no admin screen files. Admin data comes from /api/user routes. The screen names are unknown.

regressionTests.name: Create subscription with a known plan name
regressionTests.expectedResult: The call reads price, trial days, and capped amount from pricing.json. An unknown plan name throws an error.

regressionTests.name: Reject the new 20 USD and 50 USD plan names
regressionTests.expectedResult: The catalog has no 20 USD plan and no 50 USD plan. The test fails the release until those keys exist.

regressionTests.name: Return empty paywalls
regressionTests.expectedResult: The method returns an empty object for each current plan. A missing subscription uses the free-user key.

regressionTests.name: Write a free subscription on the user
regressionTests.expectedResult: The user isSubscription object gets the plan name and the base price. The call returns a return_url.

regressionTests.name: Skip usage charge when the percent is zero
regressionTests.expectedResult: charges.value 0 makes the billed amount 0. The usage charge call does not run.

regressionTests.name: Plan upgrade path
regressionTests.expectedResult: A merchant on a 0 price plan can start a paid plan that exists in pricing.json. Shopify returns a confirmation url. The new 50 USD plan is absent, so that upgrade fails.

regressionTests.name: Plan downgrade path
regressionTests.expectedResult: Cancel sets isSubscription to false. A later free subscription writes the free plan name. The theme script then receives that name.

regressionTests.name: Order limit boundary
regressionTests.expectedResult: The monthly count increments. The order still completes. No Slack limit note is sent, because monthly_store_orders is absent.

regressionTests.name: Discount cap boundary
regressionTests.expectedResult: The route accepts another discount. No counter blocks it. The release fails if the 20 USD plan must cap total discounts.

regressionTests.name: New install has no forced paid plan
regressionTests.expectedResult: Install sets UI counters. It does not set isSubscription. The free forever assignment stays commented out.

regressionTests.name: Peak day offers stay active
regressionTests.expectedResult: Existing offers still discount the cart. The functions do not read the plan. A new cap must not stop offers during the peak day until the merchant chooses the 50 USD plan.

regressionTests.name: Many offer types on the unlimited plan
regressionTests.expectedResult: Fixed bundles, frequently bought together, and quantity breaks save with no plan gate. The 50 USD plan is not in the catalog.

regressionTests.name: One or two bundles on the lower plan
regressionTests.expectedResult: The merchant can save one or two bundle types. Paywalls do not enforce a bundle count. The nearest prices in the catalog are 0 and 19, not 20.

regressionTests.name: New merchant storefront has no extra plan block
regressionTests.expectedResult: The widget loads from merchantInfo. It does not ask for a new subscription and it does not hide the offer for a missing plan.

recommendedMitigations.risk: Billing error on an unknown plan name
recommendedMitigations.mitigation: Add the new plan keys before release. Keep every old plan key. Roll back by sending merchants to an old plan name that is still in pricing.json.
Put the discount cap on the 20 USD plan paywall. Leave the 50 USD plan paywall with no cap. Alert when getPaywalls returns an empty object for a new plan.
Use a feature flag and a staged rollout. Give a grace period through peak days. Do not reset the discount counter during the grace period. There is no pricing feature flag in the code today.
Send a short plan note before the change. Staff support at the stated 20 percent occupancy. Watch Slack order-limit notes and billing errors.
Keep the 0 price plans for current merchants until they choose a new plan. Stage the new prices. Roll back to the old plan keys if paid installs fall.

recommendedMitigations.risk: Usage charge on the yearly percent plan
recommendedMitigations.mitigation: Confirm charges.value before the price change. Alert when a usage charge is above 0 for a plan that should be a flat fee.

recommendedMitigations.risk: Revenue jobs miss the new plans
recommendedMitigations.mitigation: Add the new plan names to the cron plan lists in the same release as pricing.json.
